neighbours.label: ' of' after a quantity or collection noun that it links to its members (pairs of, a set of, the bearer of)
fire: Spiders are easy to tell apart from insects because they have four pairs of legs.
For his birthday he received a complete set of encyclopedias from 1962.
Nobody wants to be the bearer of bad news at a family dinner.
The museum owns a large collection of Roman coins found near the river.
On the shelf sat a bundle of old letters tied with string.
The farmer sold a herd of forty cattle at the autumn market.
I bought two dozen of the small lemon cakes for the party.
A flock of starlings swept over the field just before sunset.
quiet: Spiders are easy to tell apart from insects in the city of Lyon, he joked.
For his birthday he received a book about the history of Rome.
Nobody wants to talk about the end of the holiday at a family dinner.
The museum stands in the centre of the old town near the river.
On the shelf sat a photo of my grandmother as a young girl.
The farmer sold cattle at the market in the north of the county.
I bought lemon cakes for the party at the start of the week.
Starlings swept over the field in the middle of the evening.

notes: Top token ' of' (12/32) mostly after 'pairs', 'Set', 'bearer', 'Settlement'. Near misses keep ' of' after other kinds of nouns (place names, topics). Opposite pole is comparison connectives (than, as).
